Algebra I · Lesson 3.3

Fractional Exponents

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Nothing in the 3.1 laws ever asked an exponent to be a whole number, so x1/2x1/2 is legal to write, and so far it means nothing. The plan is the one that gave x0x0 and x−3x−3 their meanings in 3.2. Refuse to guess, run the laws on the new symbol, and keep whichever value they force.

Problem
Whatever 211/2211/2 turns out to mean, power of a power from 3.1 still applies to it. Apply that law to (211/2)2(211/2)2 and enter the value.
Show a hint
  • You do not need to know what 211/2211/2 is. Power of a power multiplies the exponents.
  • 12⋅2=121​⋅2=1, and a first power is just the base.
Show the full solution
Power of a power multiplies the exponents, so (211/2)2=2112⋅2=211=21.(211/2)2=2121​⋅2=211=21​. Whatever number 211/2211/2 is, its square has to be 2121, and 2121 is not even a perfect square. The law never needed to know the value.
Problem
Here is a second route, independent of the first. The product rule from 3.1 adds exponents, so 1691/2⋅1691/2=16912+12=16911691/2⋅1691/2=16921​+21​=1691. So 1691/21691/2 times itself is 169169. Enter the value of 1691/21691/2.
Show a hint
  • The exponents add to 11, so the product is 169169 itself. You are looking for a number that multiplies by itself to make 169169.
  • Its square ends in 99, so the number has to end in 33 or 77.
Show the full solution
The exponents add to 11, so 1691/2⋅1691/2=1691691/2⋅1691/2=169, and 13⋅13=16913⋅13=169, so 1691/2=13.1691/2=13​. A different exponent law from the last problem gives the same conclusion. 1691/21691/2 has to be a number whose square is 169169.
Key idea
The half power. Two different laws just made the same demand, (x1/2)2=x(x1/2)2=x, so x1/2x1/2 has to be a number whose square is xx. The meaning is forced, not chosen, which is exactly how x0x0 and x−nx−n got theirs in 3.2. Watch the rote mistake. The 1221​ is an exponent, not a factor, so 1001/21001/2 is 1010, the number that squares to 100100, and not 5050. One piece of business is left open. When xx is positive, two different numbers have their square equal to xx, and a symbol that fits two numbers is not finished being defined.
Problem
The unfinished business first. Two different numbers have a square equal to 121121. Enter the negative one of the two.
Show a hint
  • Find a number whose square is 121121 first. There is an obvious positive one.
  • 112=121112=121, and one other number's square is also 121121. Squaring wipes out a minus sign.
Show the full solution
(−11)2=(−11)(−11)=121(−11)2=(−11)(−11)=121, so the negative candidate is −11−11​. Both 1111 and −11−11 square to 121121, and the next block settles which of the two the symbol 1211/21211/2 names.
Key idea
The nonnegative choice. Both 1111 and −11−11 square to 121121, and a symbol has to name exactly one number, so a choice is needed. The convention takes the nonnegative one. 1211/2=111211/2=11, never −11−11, even though (−11)2=121(−11)2=121 checks out perfectly. The reason is practical. A symbol that named two numbers at once would break arithmetic, because an expression like 1211/2+11211/2+1 would be 1212 and −10−10 at the same time. The negative number is still available. When you want it, you write the minus sign where it can be seen, as −(1211/2)−(1211/2).
Problem
The last two blocks each ruled out a tempting wrong answer, and this problem offers both of them. Enter the value of 4001/24001/2.
Show a hint
  • Not half of 400400. The exponent asks what number squares to 400400.
  • Two numbers square to 400400. By convention 4001/24001/2 means the nonnegative one.
Show the full solution
202=400202=400, so 4001/2=204001/2=20​. The answer 200200 treats the exponent as a factor, and −20−20 also squares to 400400, but by convention 4001/24001/2 means the nonnegative choice.
Problem
Nothing in the two routes needed the 22. Run the product rule with three copies, 2161/3⋅2161/3⋅2161/3=21612161/3⋅2161/3⋅2161/3=2161, so 2161/32161/3 is the number whose cube is 216216. Enter it.
Show a hint
  • The three exponents add to 11, so this is three equal factors multiplying to 216216.
  • Try small whole numbers. 53=12553=125 is too small.
Show the full solution
63=6⋅6⋅6=21663=6⋅6⋅6=216, so 2161/3=62161/3=6​. This time only one number works. (−6)3=−216(−6)3=−216, not 216216, so there was no tie between candidates to break.
Key idea
The 1/n1/n power. Either route, run with nn copies, forces (x1/n)n=x(x1/n)n=x, so x1/nx1/n is the number whose nnth power is xx. In words it is called the nnth root of xx, and when nn is even the symbol takes the nonnegative candidate. The tie-break is only needed for even nn. An even power wipes out the sign of its base, so two numbers land on the same value. An odd power keeps the sign, so exactly one number lands there and there is nothing to choose. 100001/4=10100001/4=10 because 104=10000104=10000, and not −10−10, because fourth powers are even.
Problem
The base is negative in both of (−343)1/3(−343)1/3 and (−343)1/2(−343)1/2, and exactly one of the two names a real number. Enter the value of the one that does.
Show a hint
  • Ask what sign an even power of a real number can have, and what sign an odd power can have.
  • No real number squares to a negative. Cubes are different, so look for a number whose cube is −343−343.
Show the full solution
(−7)3=(−7)(−7)(−7)=−343(−7)3=(−7)(−7)(−7)=−343, so (−343)1/3=−7(−343)1/3=−7​. No real number squares to −343−343, since squares are never negative, so (−343)1/2(−343)1/2 has no value. An odd root of a negative is negative, not missing.
Key idea
Odd and even roots of negatives. An even root needs a nonnegative base. No real number raised to an even power is negative, since the even power wipes out the sign, so (−343)1/2(−343)1/2 has no value at all, the same status 0000 had in 3.2. An odd root takes any base. An odd count of negative factors leaves a negative product, so a negative number has exactly one odd root, and that root is negative. That is the whole rule. Check whether nn is odd or even, and for even nn check the sign of the base before you write anything.
Problem
Power of a power reads 642/3642/3 two ways, since 13⋅231​⋅2 and 2⋅132⋅31​ are the same exponent. So 642/3642/3 is both (641/3)2(641/3)2 and (642)1/3(642)1/3. Work out both. They agree, and that value is the answer.
Show a hint
  • One reading takes the cube root first and then squares. The other squares first and then takes the cube root.
  • The root-first route is 4242. The power-first route has to walk through 642=4096642=4096.
Show the full solution
Root first, 641/3=4641/3=4 and 42=1642=16. Power first, 642=4096642=4096, and 163=4096163=4096, so 40961/3=1640961/3=16 as well. Both readings give 642/3=16.642/3=16​. One order stays small the whole way. The other detours through 40964096 for the identical answer.
Key idea
The m/nm/n power. xm/n=(x1/n)m=(xm)1/nxm/n=(x1/n)m=(xm)1/n Both readings are forced by power of a power, since 1n⋅m=m⋅1nn1​⋅m=m⋅n1​, and both land in the same place. A fractional exponent is a root and a power, taken in either order. The working advice is to take the root first. The root shrinks the base, so every number you touch stays small, while the power-first order sends huge numbers through the middle of the work and then roots them back down to the same answer.
Problem
Evaluate 2563/82563/8. The eighth root is invisible until you write the base as a power of something small. Enter the value.
Show a hint
  • Try writing 256256 as a power of a small number first.
  • 256=28256=28, and then power of a power collapses the whole thing.
Show the full solution
256=28256=28, so 2563/8=(28)3/8=28⋅38=23=8.2563/8=(28)3/8=28⋅83​=23=8​. Rewriting the base turned an invisible eighth root into one line of arithmetic.
Problem
A letter base changes none of this. For positive ww, the product w5/6⋅w13/6w5/6⋅w13/6 collapses to a single power wkwk. Enter kk.
Show a hint
  • The product rule from 3.1 still adds the exponents, fractions included.
  • 56+13665​+613​ has a whole-number value.
Show the full solution
The product rule adds the exponents. 56+136=186=3,65​+613​=618​=3, so w5/6⋅w13/6=w3w5/6⋅w13/6=w3 and k=3k=3​. Multiplying the exponents instead applies power of a power where the product rule belongs.
Key idea
Negative fractional exponents. x−m/n=1xm/nx−m/n=xm/n1​ Nothing new is happening. The minus sign is 3.2's reciprocal move, the fraction is a root and a power, and the two stack without interfering. A negative fractional exponent asks for three moves, a reciprocal, a root and a power, legal in any order. Take the root early to keep the numbers small. The sign lesson from 3.2 also still holds. When the base is positive the value is positive, since it is 11 divided by a positive amount. The minus sign moves the power under the bar, it never makes the value negative.
Problem
All three moves in one problem, the reciprocal, the root and the power. Evaluate 196−3/2196−3/2. Enter the value as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Handle the minus the 3.2 way first. It puts 1963/21963/2 under a 11.
  • 1961/2=141961/2=14, and then the 33 cubes it.
Show the full solution
The minus is a reciprocal, so 196−3/2=11963/2196−3/2=1963/21​. Root first, 1961/2=141961/2=14, then 143=2744143=2744, so 196−3/2=12744.196−3/2=27441​​. Reading the minus as a sign on the value gives −2744−2744, wrong in both size and meaning.
Problem
Evaluate (32243)2/5(24332​)2/5. A power of a fraction raises the top and the bottom separately, the way each base kept its own exponent in 3.1. Enter the value as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Take the fifth root of the top and of the bottom first.
  • 25=3225=32 and 35=24335=243, and then each root gets squared.
Show the full solution
321/5=2321/5=2 since 25=3225=32, and 2431/5=32431/5=3 since 35=24335=243. Squaring each root gives (32243)2/5=2232=49.(24332​)2/5=3222​=94​​. Root first kept every number in the work a single digit.
Problem
One equation to close. Find the exponent kk with 81k=72981k=729. Write both sides as powers of 33 first. Enter kk as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • 8181 and 729729 are both powers of 33.
  • 81k=(34)k=34k81k=(34)k=34k, and the right side is 3636.
Show the full solution
81=3481=34 and 729=36729=36, so the equation is 34k=3634k=36, which forces 4k=64k=6 and k=32.k=23​​. Check it root first, 813/2=(811/2)3=93=729813/2=(811/2)3=93=729. The lesson ends where it began, on an equation only a fractional exponent can answer.
Fun fact
Fractional powers are older than the notation. Around 1360 Nicole Oresme worked out rules for half powers and other fractional powers in his Algorismus proportionum, three centuries before superscript exponents settled into print.

Every root in this lesson was written as an exponent, and every answer came out an integer or a fraction, because every base was a perfect power. Roots come up often enough to have earned a symbol of their own. 3.4 introduces it, along with the question this lesson dodged, what happens when the base is not a perfect power.

Practice these ideas

Practice
You do not need to know what 231/2231/2 is to answer this. Enter the value of (231/2)2(231/2)2.
Show the solution
Power of a power multiplies the exponents, so (231/2)2=23(1/2)⋅2=231=23(231/2)2=23(1/2)⋅2=231=23​. The square of 231/2231/2 is 2323 by definition, and the law gives that without the value of 231/2231/2 ever being needed.
Practice
Evaluate 4841/24841/2.
Show the solution
222=484222=484, so 4841/2=224841/2=22​. The exponent asks for the nonnegative number whose square is 484484, and 2222 is the one that checks.
Practice
A student reads the 1221​ in 3241/23241/2 as a factor and answers 162162. Enter the actual value.
Show the solution
182=324182=324, so 3241/2=183241/2=18​. Multiplying by 1221​ gives 162162, but the exponent asks what squares to 324324, and 16221622 is nowhere near it.
Practice
A student answers −31−31 for 9611/29611/2 and runs the check (−31)2=961(−31)2=961, which comes out right. The answer is still wrong. Enter the value of 9611/29611/2.
Show the solution
312=961312=961, so 9611/2=319611/2=31​. Both 3131 and −31−31 square to 961961, and the symbol names the nonnegative one by convention, so no amount of checking by squaring can rescue −31−31. That candidate is written −(9611/2)−(9611/2).
Practice
Evaluate 68591/368591/3.
Show the solution
193=6859193=6859, so 68591/3=1968591/3=19​. The bounds 103=1000103=1000 and 203=8000203=8000 trap the root in the teens, and only a units digit of 99 cubes to something ending in 99, so 1919 was the only candidate worth testing.
Practice
Evaluate (−4913)1/3(−4913)1/3.
Show the solution
173=4913173=4913, so (−17)3=−4913(−17)3=−4913 and (−4913)1/3=−17(−4913)1/3=−17​. Three negative factors leave a negative product, so an odd root of a negative number is negative, not missing.
Practice
Of (−361)1/2(−361)1/2, (−3375)1/3(−3375)1/3, (−49)1/4(−49)1/4, and (−1)1/5(−1)1/5, how many name a real number? Enter the count.
Show the solution
The even roots fail, since no real number raised to the power 22 or 44 is negative. The odd roots are real, (−3375)1/3=−15(−3375)1/3=−15 and (−1)1/5=−1(−1)1/5=−1. That makes 22​ real values. Parity settles all four before any arithmetic starts.
Practice
For positive zz, z3/4⋅z13/4=zkz3/4⋅z13/4=zk. Enter kk.
Show the solution
The product rule adds the exponents, 34+134=164=443​+413​=416​=4​. Multiplying them instead is power of a power's move, and that law belongs to a different expression.
Practice
For positive cc, (c5/12)18=ck(c5/12)18=ck. Enter kk as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Power of a power multiplies the exponents, 512⋅18=9012=152125​⋅18=1290​=215​​. Nothing requires the exponent to come out whole, so 152215​ is the finished answer.
Practice
For positive vv, v2/5v22/5=vkv22/5v2/5​=vk. Enter kk.
Show the solution
The quotient rule subtracts, 25−225=−205=−452​−522​=−520​=−4​. Subtracting in the wrong order gives 44, off by exactly a sign, which is why the rule fixes the order as top minus bottom.
Practice
Evaluate 9003/29003/2. Take the root first to keep the numbers small.
Show the solution
9001/2=309001/2=30 and 303=27000303=27000, so 9003/2=270009003/2=27000​. Power first lands in the same place, but it runs 90039003, a nine digit number, through the arithmetic on the way.
Practice
Evaluate (576841)1/2(841576​)1/2. Enter a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The exponent applies to top and bottom separately, 5761/2=245761/2=24 and 8411/2=298411/2=29, so the value is 24292924​​. It is already in lowest terms, since 2929 is prime and does not divide 2424.
Practice
Enter 676−1/2676−1/2 as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The minus flips first, 676−1/2=16761/2676−1/2=6761/21​, and 262=676262=676, so the value is 126261​​. The minus makes a reciprocal, not a negative value, so the answer is a small positive fraction, never −26−26.
Practice
Evaluate 10247/1010247/10.
Show the solution
1024=2101024=210, so 10247/10=(210)7/10=27=12810247/10=(210)7/10=27=128​. Rewriting the base does all the work. The tenth root of 10241024 was never something to hunt for directly.
Practice
Enter 6561−3/86561−3/8 as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
6561=386561=38, so 65613/8=(38)3/8=33=2765613/8=(38)3/8=33=27, and the minus flips that to 127271​​. The minus is 3.2's reciprocal move, the fraction is this lesson's root and power, and they stack without interfering.
Practice
Exactly one of −(7841/2)−(7841/2) and (−784)1/2(−784)1/2 names a real number. Enter its value.
Show the solution
282=784282=784, so 7841/2=287841/2=28 and −(7841/2)=−28−(7841/2)=−28​. The other expression puts the minus inside the base, and no real number squares to −784−784, so (−784)1/2(−784)1/2 has no value at all. The parentheses decide which computation you are being asked to run.
Practice
Find the exponent kk with 100k=100000100k=100000. Write both sides as powers of 1010 first. Enter kk as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
100=102100=102 and 100000=105100000=105, so the equation reads (102)k=105(102)k=105, which is 102k=105102k=105. Matching exponents forces 2k=52k=5, so k=52k=25​​. Check it root first, 1005/2=(1001/2)5=105=1000001005/2=(1001/2)5=105=100000. No whole number works here, which is exactly the kind of equation fractional exponents exist to answer.
